title: Chosen, So Held to Account
overview: Amos tells Israel that being close to God makes them more accountable, not less, and warns that their wealthy capital, Samaria, will fall because of its cruelty to the poor.

parts.label: Chosen means accountable (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: God reminds Israel that he brought them out of Egypt and knew them closely, like family. The surprise is the conclusion: because they were that close, he will hold them to account for every wrong.

parts.label: Every effect has a cause (vv. 3-6)
parts.note: A string of everyday questions about walkers, lions, bird traps and alarm trumpets all make one point: nothing happens without a cause. Amos applies it bluntly, saying that when disaster strikes a city the LORD is behind it, a claim many readers find hard.

parts.label: Why the prophet must speak (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: Amos says God warns through his prophets before he acts, so the people are not caught without notice. Just as a lion's roar makes everyone afraid, he says he cannot keep quiet once God has spoken.

parts.label: Foreigners called as witnesses (vv. 9-11)
parts.note: Leaders of Ashdod, a Philistine city, and of Egypt are invited onto the hills around Samaria to look at the turmoil and oppression inside. The powerful have filled their fortified homes with what they took by force, so an enemy will strip those same homes, which most readers link to Assyria's capture of Samaria around 722 BC.

parts.label: Only scraps rescued (v. 12)
parts.note: A shepherd whose sheep was killed by a lion could bring back a leg or a bit of ear as proof to the owner, so this 'rescue' is grim irony. Only scraps of Samaria's comfortable rich and their fine furniture will be left, though the exact words about the couch are hard to translate and scholars are unsure.

parts.label: Altars and mansions fall (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: Bethel held a royal shrine with a golden calf, and the horns on an altar's corners were where someone in danger could grab hold for safety, so cutting them off means there is no refuge. The rich owned separate winter and summer homes decorated with carved ivory, pieces of which archaeologists have found at Samaria, and all of it will be torn down.

disagreement: Christians differ on how far verse 6 reaches: some take it to mean God directly causes every disaster, while others read it as speaking only of the specific judgment Amos is announcing on Israel.
think: Do you think having more advantages or closer relationships should mean being held to a higher standard than others, and why?
